utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'd like to deal with a few procedural issues before we give an opportunity to the Prosecution to call its next witness. The first, I think I yesterday asked the Simatovic view on scheduling around Orthodox Christmas. It might be that you had been clear on that already and that you would prefer to sit on the 10th, 11th and 12th, that is Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday after the court recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but first of all I would like to apologise. Yesterday you told us that you wanted us to send you a mail. Unfortunately we have just forgotten to do that, we can do it subsequently or perhaps we can do it now verbally. If the Trial Chamber is of the opinion that this is doable, the 10th, 11th and 12th would be okay and we know that the 12th might not be doable but if it can be done, even in the afternoon that would be okay and once again which apologise for not sending you an e-mail as you requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. As far as the Chamber is concerned, the Chamber has decided that it, depending on practical matters, such as availability of courtrooms, et cetera, but that the Chamber is willing to adapt the schedule in such a way that we'll sit on the 10th, the 11th and the 12th of January and we'll try, but that depends on the Perisic case, and we'll try to sit on Wednesday morning, but if not possible then we'll sit in the afternoon. Again this is to be verified with CMSS, but the Chamber has made up its mind. The Chamber has received scheduling for December. For the 13th to the 15th of December, witness JF-056 has been scheduled and we see, Mr. Groome, that you also had scheduled a witness for the 16th of December, which would be the fourth witness that week. Now, in view of the medical report the Chamber receives today, there seems at least to be no medical objections against four days a week apart from other objections. No medical objections for four days a week, and the Chamber is inclined to agree with that schedule which would then be four days in that week. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only rise to remind Your Honours of the submission we made concerning the opinion about four days a week and what we submitted was absent from that assessment, which we felt was important, if not essential for that assessment. On the other hand, our objections to the four days was directed at a continuous four-day-a-week programme and if it's only suggested four days a week for one week, we probably wouldn't need to address Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At this moment we are discussing this one week, which leaves alone that, of course, that the Chamber might consider, but then we'll give you a further opportunity to address the Chamber, if we would move to four days a week on a more permanent basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just may remind the Chamber that there are there is at least one unresolved matter with respect to JF-051 that needs to be resolved before he is called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll pay attention to that. Then next item I read out a statement on behalf of the Chamber yesterday in relation to Mr. Kovacevic, more or less between two sentences, Mr. Jordash expressed that he did not, at least the not at that moment, want to make any comments. I don't know whether now, having more time, whether it was just due to the circumstances yesterday or that you had no comments to be made?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No comments, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No comments. I haven't asked -- I see, Mr. Bakrac that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections from the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then that matter is -- stands as I stated yesterday. Then we have for Witness JF-057 admission of related exhibits. Madam Registrar has filed a memorandum in which she lists the exhibits by their 65 ter numbers, the proposed exhibit numbers, the description of those exhibits, and in the last column whether they are confidential or not. It ranges from P01629 up to and including P01653. Two out of that range have already been admitted into evidence, that is P1647 and P1649. When will the Chamber hear of any objections, if any?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May we indicate by the end of the week. As I recall, I don't think we have any, but I'd like to double-check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac, same for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same for us, Your Honours. I would like to check first but I don't think we'll have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber sets as a time-limit the 3rd of December, that is Friday close of business, for any objections to be made. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one kind of technical matter related to one of these I'd like to bring to your attention. It relates to P1632. It is an exhibit from the Milosevic case and is tendered as an associate exhibit. In this case, the version we uploaded in e-court was signed by the witness and bears the ERN 0291-0458, 0291-0464. An alert member of my staff spotted that it appears that Mr. Nice in the Milosevic case, through some inadvertent oversight used a version of this exhibit that was not the final version. The text is exactly the same and the only difference is that the font on the final ERN version is larger. There is no practical difference between the two exhibits other than in one case, Mr. Nice refers to a specific name, Kajman, and adds the information that the name appears as the third name from the bottom. This can be found at the bottom page T-09420. If the Chamber simply ignores Mr. Nice's reference of the third name from the bottom, the Chamber will have a correct understanding of what the witness said about P1632 in her Milosevic case testimony. Or in the alternative, we can replace the current P1632 with an exact version as found in the JDB database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At my age, I would prefer the larger fonts as a matter of fact, but I do understand that it gives a different picture. Could the Defence teams include these comments. If there's any objection against this version with the larger font but with exactly the same content then we'd like to know, otherwise, Mr. Groome, the Chamber will consider to admit the exhibit as it is uploaded now. Thank you for this comment. Next item, the Nielsen report. The Chamber has received a courtesy copy of I don't know whether it's filed already but at least a notice of withdrawal of witness Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, it was filed yesterday evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was filed yesterday evening. Then I hereby put on the record that all motions in relation to this witness are hereby declared moot. We might specify them in the near future, but I already pronounce them to be moot. The instruction to the Registry in relation to the pre-assignment of exhibit numbers is hereby also lifted because it doesn't serve any purpose anymore. Any questions or comments in relation to this? If not, we move to the next item. Madam Registrar, the Chamber would like you to assign exhibit numbers for any outstanding documents that have not yet been tendered or MFI'd in relation to the testimony of Mr. Theunens. The Prosecution has filed the table and the Defence teams have filed their comments on the content of the table, so it's now time to pre-assign numbers to the documents found in that table which, as I said before, are still outstanding. Then last item, Mr. Jordash, yesterday you indicated that you needed urgently an order from the Chamber, an order to have the Victims and Witness Section submit audio recordings to Witness JF-026. We received a message from VWS that they were a bit surprised because there had been no request, at least they were not aware of it. Perhaps I'm not going to -- any request to -- prior to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We got a notification from the Prosecution that VWS were not willing to do that. I think I'm speaking correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's clarified. Mr. Groome, you informed --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I informed Mr. Jordash that last week I asked -- we made that request of VWS and they said they were unwilling. They did not think it was appropriate for VWS to hand a witness documents from a party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that the misunderstanding may have been resolved by your observation and the confirmation by Mr. Groome. I leave it to that for the time being. I have no other matters on my list. Then the next witness will testify with pseudonym, face and voice distortion from what I remember. Mr. Groome, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That conforms with my understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then are all the protective measures in place? If so, may the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is being escorted, this witness has expressed in previous testimony some concern about his identity being revealed. I have taken the liberty of including the two cases which this witness has given evidence before on the pseudonym sheet and I would ask if the Court Officer could hand a courtesy copy to the Chamber of the pseudonym sheet at this point. I've already provided it to the Defence. It is my suggestion that if myself and counsel on the Defence refer to the cases as case number 1 and case number 2, we can give full effect to the protections ordered by the Chamber. And finally I would ask that a paper copy be left in front of the witness so it also would serve as a reminder to him which case we are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber has received the courtesy copy you have provided to the Registry, so we are aware of the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I earlier referred to the table of the Theunens documents, it was, I mentioned the Prosecution table but both filings of course are received, that is the Stanisic and Simatovic Defence. Good afternoon, Witness JF-026. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by the usher. I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Witness JF-026. Witness JF-026, I call you by that pseudonym because we'll not use your own name in court. Apart from that, your face cannot be seen by the outside world, neither can your own voice be heard by the outside world. Face is distorted and your voice is distorted in our communications with outsiders. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Groome. Mr. Groome is counsel for the Prosecution and you'll find him on your right. Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: JF-026, you are here today pursuant to a subpoena issued by this Trial Chamber on the 15th of October, 2010; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You did not come voluntarily here?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I didn't come voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, JF-026, prior to your arrival in The Hague, I was informed by representatives of the Victims Witness Services, that you did not want to meet with myself or any staff member of the Office of the Prosecutor, did they inform me correctly?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So prior to coming to court today, you did not have any contact with any member of the OTP staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Judge Orie has just described the protective measures that have been provided for you. I would just add one note, that because of voice distortion, I would ask that you do not start your answer until the question is completed so that we may turn off our microphones and that your voice is truly distorted. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that 65 ter 5869 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: JF-026, you should on the right-hand screen before you see what we refer to as a pseudonym sheet. Can I ask you, is that your name and date of birth on this sheet?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: To give full effect to the protective measures ordered for you, we will not refer to the date or the cases in which you previously testified. Can I ask you to review the date of the statement and the two cases listed on this sheet and indicate to us are those cases in which you previously appeared?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender the following exhibit under seal and ask that a paper copy be placed in front of the witness for reference during the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 5869 becomes Exhibit P1654 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1654 is admitted under seal. Mr. Groome, you didn't indicate that it should not be shown to the public, of course, in view of the kind of document that goes without saying, but may I ask for precision in respect of exhibits that will still follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, JF-026, because you refused to meet with me, I'm not sure which topics I may ask you about you may feel might identify you. If at any time you are asked a question which you believe would reveal your identity if you gave a complete and honest answer in open court, I ask that you bring that to the attention of the Chamber. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do see that you express concerns about your identity having become public. First of all, when did you write and perhaps I'm also looking at you, Mr. Groome, whether you are aware of any correspondence on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I know that this witness had made this situation known to the Office of the Prosecutor. I cannot cite the manner in which that was done or the specific correspondent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what in response the Office of the Prosecutor did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was my intention to speak with the witness about this. As you know, he has refused to speak with me. I do not know what Victim Witness has done with respect to this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us, witness, when did you write letters in relation to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My identity was disclosed on several occasions and my lawyer addressed the OTP on the 24th of September, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And did you address the matter more recently, well, let's say this year in any correspondence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did. After my testimony in

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I direct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question is whether you brought it to the attention of the Tribunal, which would be the first most appropriate instance to consider such concerns.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. I have a written document based on which I drew their attention to this. I did this every time orally and in writing through my lawyer. I don't know of any other way to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you point at any specific instance during the last year where you have tried to contact, either directly or through your lawyer, the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before Judge Dilparic at the special court in Belgrade. I don't know exactly who represented the Tribunal there, but my witness is Judge Dilparic who was present during these discussions before the special court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you discuss the matter with the Victims and Witness Section recently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I sent them a letter the other day, and I asked to have a meeting with them before my testimony here. However, upon hearing that I did not wish to have contacts with the OTP, they said that that would have contacts with me after my testimony and they did not even want to carry or take upon themselves the course of my stay on the 27th here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you send them a letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several days ago. I have a copy here. On the 24th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was last week, Wednesday. Could you provide a copy of that letter to the Registrar so that we can first of all see in what language it's stated, that it can be copied, and that the parties will have access to that letter. I suggest to the parties that the letter, the letter being in B/C/S, be copied. It's a handwritten copy apparently of a letter. Meanwhile we'll verify whether this letter has been received by VWS and what in response to that has been undertaken. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have any meeting with any representative of the Victims and Witness Section recently, Witness JF-026?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they told me that they would be in touch with me after my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you asked to meet with them before your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had earlier agreed that we would meet yesterday, but then it turned out that they told me that we would meet at the end of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they give any reason why they did not meet with you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't give any reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you make yourself available yesterday to meet with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've been here since the 27th and I've been waiting to hear from them if we would meet or not. The only answer I ultimately got from them was that we would meet at the end of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where would you meet yesterday? At what time and at what place, and you don't have to describe the address, but, for example, in your hotel or in the Tribunal? So find a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was ready yesterday at 5.00 p.m. in my hotel. They were supposed to come and pick me up and take me to the office here, but they postponed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ask for such a postponement or did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was available waiting. They suggested that we should meet afterwards. I don't know if my understanding of what they said was correct, that apparently they were not allowed to talk to me until the end of my testimony or perhaps I misunderstood it, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will pay further attention to what you just said and we'll verify the information with the Victims and Witness Section. Now, there's one issue, I do understand that you did not make yourself available to meet with Mr. Groome or one of his colleagues. To whom did you tell that you would not be available to meet with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that letter, I addressed the Victims and Witnesses Section and told them so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was any material given to you to review, whether audio material or whatever material, from your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday evening or yesterday afternoon at around 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it given to you by someone of the Victims and Witness Section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you finally met with them yesterday although briefly. What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you consider a brief encounter with a driver of the Victims and Witnesses Section who brought the material over to me in the hotel, if you consider that a meeting, that was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not specifically say meeting. I said you met with them and you have now clarified that you only received some material. We'll verify this information. Now, witness, let's go back to the issue where we are, that is your testimony. I do understand that you are reluctant to give evidence. Do you think that in view of the fact that you say that your identity was revealed earlier, do you want any further protection than you have at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes and no because my wish is not to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has anyone explained to you that there's a civil duty, also a duty under the rules of this Tribunal that once called as a witness and you are not just called but even subpoenaed to appear as a witness, that you are under a duty to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read the order and the representatives of the police from Belgrade who brought the order and served it on me explained it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I -- being aware that you are under a duty to testify and that not answering -- willfully not answering questions exposes you to contempt proceedings, and I again repeat the question whether although you would rather not testify, whether in the present circumstances you want the protective measures to be extended? And what remains is as a possibility, I'm not saying that it will be granted, but what would remain apart from the protective measures already in place would be to give your testimony in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I must testify, then I would prefer to do so with protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, protective measures are in place at this moment, as I explained to you earlier. That is that no one sees your face, that no one hears your own voice, and that we are not using your own name, although the content of your testimony, unless that testimony would reveal your identity, would be public. That is what is in place and do I understand your answer that you would like this to be extended to giving your testimony in closed session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would rather not testify at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear, but at this moment we are discussing where you are under a duty to testify whether you want to have your protective measures extended beyond what is already in place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain a bit in further detail what concerns you have in respect of your safety or safety of your family members, and you referred earlier to your identity having become known after your previous testimony. Could you tell us what happened, what effect it had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, it's very difficult to explain the situation because it is down to delicate details. It's not that my personal safety is threatened, but it's the sort of Gandhi-esque resistance in that the society, the community where I live refuses to accept, to have in its midst people who testify before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you explain what the community around you has conveyed to you in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the message that I got after my first appearance before the Tribunal was given to me through the two-year ban on entry to Serbia that followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that ban was lifted when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was never officially imposed. There was no decision to that effect. I would merely be told to turn back whenever I wanted to cross the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And were you able to return to Serbia at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us one example of the harassment you experienced after the second testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The business I run, well, there was a tender for office premises where I would actually win the tender, but then it would be taken over by the town authorities, that's an example of how things would work out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that's a matter which is very difficult to verify at this very moment. Do you have any other example which needs less thorough investigations into the matter in order to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Judge. I tried to explain my position, the position where both in Serbia and

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that it's your position

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 26, I briefly consulted with my colleagues. My first observation is that if you would have met with Mr. Groome, then your concerns would have been brought to the attention of this Chamber in a way most likely which would have facilitated any decision-making in this respect. Second, it seems to this Chamber that although you would prefer to have an extended protective measures, that you do not know exactly how to appropriately raise this matter, you apparently are not sufficiently aware of the criteria that would be applied in reaching any decision on this matter, and, therefore, on the basis of what you've told us now, the Chamber is hesitant at this moment to extend any protective measures. But, we'd also like to, after having consulted with the Defence, with the parties, the Chamber is inclined to give you an opportunity to briefly discuss these matters in an efficient way with the Prosecution, and I'm now looking at the Defence, the examination has not really started, and this might lead to a relevant application, a meaningful application for extension of protective measures, which we could then consider. At the same time, the Chamber would be in a position to seek further information from the Victims and Witness Section on what you told us about your communications with that unit until now. This would allow us to consider the matter in a more meaningful way, and then to decide whether we'll continue with your examination either with extended or with the present protective measures. Mr. Groome, you are on your feet, I presented it in a rather open way in order to give the parties an opportunity as well to briefly comment on what I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have not spoken with this witness, so I don't know exactly why he refused to meet with the Prosecution, but it has been my experience that witnesses similarly situated to this witness, that their problems are only exacerbated if it becomes known that they have actually met with the Office of the Prosecutor. I do know this witness. He is -- was the first witness to come forward and attempt to assist the Tribunal with respect to events in Zvornik. He did that many years ago. I do know generally that he has come under pressure. I wonder if an alternative course of action might be to inquire whether he'd be willing to proceed provisionally in closed session and then give the Chamber an opportunity to be fully informed by Victim Witness Unit to direct them to do a proper threat assessment, to make inquiries with this witness, and then report back to the Chamber, that might have the virtue of allowing us to proceed today and the Chamber could reserve its ultimate decision on the protections until it has all the relevant information before it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I hear from the Defence how they respond to the suggestion just raised by Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just briefly consult, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We agree with Mr. Groome. We think the witness has got concerns, as he has expressed them. These things are subtle and if the witness is given an opportunity perhaps with VWS to set out his concerns, they may well turn out to be genuine and objectively based, and we would be concerned to proceed without giving him the protection he asks for until that assessment proves that he doesn't require that protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't have any problem with the protective measures for the witness that he deems necessary. It would be most useful for everybody if this witness shared his concerns with the Victims and Witnesses Unit and not with the OTP. I believe that the best advice for this witness would be provided by that service and not by the OTP. I believe that this would be the best course of action for everybody concerned and not only for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Let me just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-026, I've consulted with my colleagues. The Chamber follows the suggestion given by Mr. Groome, which means that we will hear your evidence in closed session, meaning that the content of your testimony will be confidential, apart from that no one will use your name. At the same time, face and voice distortion will remain in place so that we finally will decide on whether your confidentiality will remain confidential not after you have explained in more detail the reasons for your request for an extension of your protection to the Victims and Witness Section, and the Chamber will take care that any possible misunderstandings about whether or not to meet with them, at what time, where to meet with them, making yourself available is -- are avoided. The Chamber nevertheless during the next break, unless the parties would object to that, then of course we would consider that again, the Chamber would like to verify some of the information the witness has given as to the communication over the last week to say. I see that all teams apparently agree with the Chamber seeking verification. Whether that will be by a telephone call or by inviting the relevant persons of the Victims and Witness Section to meet with the Judges or one of the Judges is still to be decided. We'll proceed, Witness JF-026, therefore, in closed session. Mr. Groome will now start his examination. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one additional matter before I continue with my examination. I would note this witness has mentioned two cases --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it doesn't make that much of a difference, we move into closed session at this moment. Mr. Groome, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that a hard copy of the pseudonym sheet be placed before the witness so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: JF-026, do you have a hard copy of the pseudonym sheet that you saw on the screen earlier? Do you have a sheet like this on the table before you?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could ask that you keep that on the top so when I refer to cases, I'll do so without mentioning the case. My first question to you is did you give evidence in the case indicated on the pseudonym sheet as case number 1 on the days also indicated on that pseudonym sheet?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this evidence prior to coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was informed by the Victim Witness unit that you already had in your possession audiotapes from that case and you would take it upon yourself to review that. Is that information incorrect?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Not correct. The only thing I have is an audiotape from a case number 2 on this sheet. I have that audiotape. I believe that I have it here upstairs in the office, but that's only an audiotape from case number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I then ask, did there come a time --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Or could I ask that 65 ter 5865 be placed on the screen before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you provided a statement to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in 2008?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the statement 5865 which would he see on the screens before us, is that a copy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this statement prior to giving evidence here today?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yes, this is more or less what I stated, summarised in some hundred bullet points.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you last reviewed this statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are there any corrections or clarifications you wish to make to it?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: The statement contains everything that I stated, but I would have to look at it more carefully. This is just a summary which contains perhaps 200 sentences, not more. But this is indeed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that it doesn't seem that the witness has properly reviewed the material, I have the binder with me that I had asked he be given. It contains this statement in his own language and it also contains the transcript from the first case in his own language that has because of a recent project now available in B/C/S in hard copy. I would ask that the witness be directed to review this over the course of the break and I appreciate it may take longer than the break, but so that we can proceed with my inquiry with respect to this prior evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I first ask the following question to the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: your statement, yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I don't know. I said that I had read this statement. This statement contains 114 bullet points and I really don't know what may be unclear about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My first question, when you reviewed that, did you find anything, although perhaps it might not reflect every detail of your answers, but did you find anything which you considered to be not correct? Was there at any moment anything you read you said either this is not what I intended to say, or although I said it, it's not true? Was there any such moment when you read that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was reading this statement and being aware why I had been subpoenaed, I can say that this is my statement, but the statement needs additional clarifications. Some people are mentioned here and the years, I'm mentioning people here and the questions were was he member of that or this or that organisation, but nobody ever asked me about any time-frame. This needs to be clarified. Everything that is contained in this statement is true, but the statement needs further clarifications, similar to the clarifications that I provided in the previous cases. Whenever I mention something, I believe that the time-frame is very important. And, Judge, if I may say something else, some people are mentioned and the question was, was he a minister, and I answered yes, but he was not a minister at the time when things happened in 1992. The person, for example, became minister in 1998. And somebody who is not familiar with the entire situation can gain a completely erroneous expression by just reading this statement because the times of the events happening or people being appointed to certain positions are not mentioned in this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Witness JF-026, if you were asked whether someone was a minister, for example, without a time-frame, and if you have answered that that person was, then without any time-frame, the Chamber would, of course, never believe that that person had been a minister from birth until he deceased, so therefore that goes without saying that that needs further clarification. But I do understand that you say there's -- we'll find ways to add to your statement further details which you consider to be relevant for a better understanding of your statement. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Mr. Petrovic, you are both on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are complications here which I think Your Honours are not aware of. Number one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these complications appropriately being dealt with in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we understand that the witness's difficulties when being asked these questions because of what we know about, one, the way in which this statement was compiled, and, two, we also know from subsequent evidence the witness has given in which he has offered clarifications about this statement compiled by the Prosecution from a suspect interview. So we understand and support the witness in the expression of his difficulties and we think perhaps Your Honours should be made aware of the way in which this statement came into being, and also the way in which the witness clarified this statement and whether, therefore, once Your Honours have that information, whether in fact we ought to be addressing Your Honours about whether Rule 92 ter and admission through that rule is in fact appropriate in these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I would like to address the Trial Chamber briefly. The facts presented by the witness with regard to his testimony in case 1 and the written statement that he provided, it seems to me that his statement points clearly to the fact that this witness cannot be heard as a 92 ter witness based on previous statements, old statements, and corrections that the witness may have done or may have not done. Maybe he did not have any technical possibilities to do them, maybe he didn't have the time to make corrections. The OTP should hear the witness as a viva voce witness because this is the only way we can proceed under the circumstances that have been presented to us here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, would you please respond to what the Defence teams have raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think there's one misstatement of fact that needs to be corrected. The statement is actually done after the testimony in

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: rather than deal with the different precursors to the written evidence submitted in that case, directed the Prosecution to come up with a composite of the witnesses's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You wish to refer to the first case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am sorry. A large part of what's in the statement is taken from the first case which was done viva voce and which the witness just has not had an opportunity to review. So I don't accept that 92 ter is impossible. I think because of the situation that we find ourselves in, JF-026 has not had the opportunity to review that evidence. I have the binder of not only the viva voce testimony from the first case, in that binder I have all of the associated exhibits in the original and the language the witness can understand, plus I have his statement in his own language. My suggestion would be that the witness be asked over the course of the break to review this material or get as far as he can, and to make notes in the margin of where he believes clarifications are necessary and then upon returning we would go through those clarifications one by one until we finish the 92 ter process. If we were to proceed viva voce, it would essentially be me reading the questions that I asked this witness many years ago, that I'm now seeking to tender 92 ter to avoid that unnecessary use of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask a question to the witness. Witness 26, when you testified in the first case, did you tell the truth to the best of your recollection on any matter that you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, you have to understand that I had been very close to all the events. I was on location. I'm mentioned people who are now prosecutors in Bosnia-Herzegovina and we were all afraid at the time and we all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I had a rather simple question, whether or not you did tell the truth when you testified in the first case to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's impossible to answer with just yes or no. I'm telling you that we all wanted to grovel up to the OTP, we mentioned names, we dropped names in order to save ourselves. We had been very close to the events in our local midst; that's a notorious fact. Second of all, at the moment when Hague issued all of the indictments, we didn't know what would happen and we were all under pressure, we all felt blackmailed when all the indictments were issued, the situation changed, the tables turned. It may sound a bit silly now, but that's how things were. And if you want me to testify in these proceedings, I would like to answer questions about certain individuals. I gave my solemn declaration to speak the truth and I would like to do that. I met with the OTP some 20 times in all sorts of ways. I don't want this to be mentioned in these proceedings and that's why I wrote in my letter that I didn't want to meet with the gentleman from the Office of the Prosecutor before this trial. And finally, I would like to be a witness of the Court. I was subpoenaed to be a witness of the Court and I don't want to be a witness of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, even if you are called by the Prosecution or called by the Defence, witnesses have only one duty, to tell to the Court what the truth is, so to that extent although the selection of a witness may differ from one party it to another, but once you are in this courtroom, you are a witness - although called by one of the parties - a witness of the truth, and it's the truth the Chamber is seeking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will proceed as follows: Mr. Jordash, we'll hear, but not immediately, any submissions you would like to make in relation to the statement given by the witness in 2008. You'll have an opportunity to do that. Meanwhile, Witness JF-026, you will have a break already now. You are invited to read again to the extent possible and tell us after the break the statement, the 114 bullet points, as you said, and after the break to tell us not the portions that may need clarification at this moment, but first of all to tell us where in this 114 bullet points you find something which you consider to be wrong, not to be in accordance with the truth. So either that you didn't say it, or not said a similar thing, or that although you may have said it, that it's nevertheless not true. You are invited to do that over the next -- a little bit over half an hour. Meanwhile, the Chamber will hear further submissions from the parties. Is that clear, witness? Do you have something to write?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you are invited to follow the usher and to do what I asked you to do. I add to this that it would have saved a lot of time if this all would have been done already before you appeared in court because it takes now an enormous amount of time, but that's the situation we are in. We would have appreciated this to have been done before you came to the courtroom. Could you please follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm also looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's what I was going to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time, if you want the Chamber to proceed after the break, if there's one or two minutes which you could explain what apparently your concerns are, I'm also looking at Mr. Stanisic, we also could have a break in a couple of minutes, because it then allows us to further think about the present situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In a nutshell, I think the problem is this: That this witness has provided evidence on a number of occasions in a number of ways. Off the top of my head, it's probably in excess of six or seven different modes of providing detailed evidence. It's taken me several days just to get through it all and to annotate and work out what the witness has said on different occasions, there are many differences. And so we are concerned that the way we are proceeding, trying to admit the evidence pursuant to 92 ter is -- is artificial because even the request for the witness to sit down and look at this statement in our submission makes -- and offer up what he now says is inaccurate or in need of clarification is a somewhat artificial exercise because he couldn't possibly in our submission, do it in the next half an hour, hour, or even probably in a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's also the reason why I phrased my instruction to the witness not to tell us what needed further clarification, but just what is wrong, either I didn't say it or didn't say a similar thing, as I said, or it's wrong although I may have said it. Which excludes for the time being, and I'm not yet at the point of finally deciding on admission of this statement, but at least focuses first of all on clear elements in his statement which are not in accordance with the truth, if you need further clarifications, they are not untruthful but they are not fully understandable or that they are -- so let's take it step by step. And I do see the issue you raise, but you said the way in which the statement was produced, you would like to address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, it's a bit unclear from what I've read exactly how the statement was produced, but what it does appear to me is that it was produced from both the evidence in trial 1 and also his -- the witness 's suspect interview, and it's, in our submission, a pretty selective collation, it has things which I would -- was surprised had been missed out personally. And so to ask the witness to be looking at the statement and to -- this creates the added difficulty that it was created by someone else and put before him. The witness has just clarified the pressure he felt under to give the Prosecution something useful and so again it -- we are one step in our submission, further away from 92 ter and again putting the witness, in our submission, under pressure which will only in our submission lead to further inaccuracies and thirdly, can I very briefly say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Given what the witness has said, we may well be heading in a situation where Your Honours may feel you have to warn the witness about self-incrimination and that is an added difficulty. Those are just my initial thoughts, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic, anything to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, only one point, I support everything my colleague Mr. Jordash has said. Now, a statement which covers several years, dozens of people and events cannot be checked in terms of the witness pointing to what was true and what was not true from amongst the things he said. So I join my learned friend Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, so the record is accurate about the witness's opportunity to read the statement, it's not that he would be just looking at it for the first time. When the witness indicated through VWS that he would decline to meet anyone from the OTP, I had prepared a binder of his prior evidence and asked VWS to hand it to him. When they said that they would not, I asked would they inquire of the witness whether he would receive a binder of his prior evidence so that he could read it in advance of his appearing here today. On the 28th, I received the following e-mail from VWS: "For your information when our staff informed the witness that statements would be handed out to him tomorrow, Monday, he informed us that it is not necessary to meet Rita Pradan as he already has the statement from his testimony, both in hard copy and on the CD, he has been listening to his testimony prior to the arrival in the Hague. He also has a laptop with him and will continue to listen to it before appearing at court." So I took from that that he was actively engaged in not only

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you the Chamber will consider how to proceed. We'll take a break first, I apologise for having such a long first session. We resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the parties have had an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the letter the witness has sent by fax to the Victims and Witness Section.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-026, we verified with the Victims and Witness Section during the break the communications of the last week. First of all, I was informed that the Victims and Witness Section had responded to your letter, that the fax connections were unstable at the time and that for that reason in a telephone conversation they read their answer to you and that they agreed that they would send that telefax the next day when you were close to your fax machine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that your observation that you never received an answer is not very accurate. In that response, it will be made available to the parties at a later stage -- well, as you may have noticed, the first and the second issues are of a rather practical nature. The third one, the last one, I just summarised the response. The response is that this Tribunal's mandate does not make it competent to either facilitate nor that the Tribunal has no power, and also that it's not within its competence to facilitate issuing any EU citizenship or that of the United States of America, for any witness or their family members. And the last line is: "Should you have any security concerns, the VWS protection unit will be available to discuss them with you when you arrive. Please inform" and then the name of the officer present upon arrival is mentioned. "Please inform" that person "if you would like to meet with a protection officer." I was informed that upon arrival you informed the relevant officer of the Victims and Witness Section that you wished to see a protection officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They then informed me that they tried to make -- to arrange for a meeting with you on Monday but that you were not available because you were shopping with your family and that therefore no meeting could be arranged on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what, in your view, then happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had agreed that I would be waiting for them yesterday at 5.00 p.m. and that we would discuss the issue of the -- with the protection officer, but they informed me that it would be postponed for the end of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's about yesterday. I'm talking about the day before yesterday, Monday. Did you make yourself available on Monday to meet with a protection officer or were you busy shopping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was available on Monday. However, they told me that I would meet with them on Tuesday at 5.00 p.m., but it's not true that on Monday I wasn't available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll continue. So therefore there's a divergence in the story. I was then informed that they contacted you on Tuesday where you were called on your mobile phone and you apparently were in town and that you asked to meet between 3.00 and 4.00; is that accurate information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They then, as I was told, they then brought to your attention that a meeting between 3.00 and 4.00 would create a logistical problem and whether you agreed to meet after your testimony and that you then consented to that proposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also do understand that you did not insist at that moment to say, no, I really need to see you before my testimony, but that you did not express any further security concerns at that moment apart from the reference in the letter just saying that your identity was published in 2003, that you did not express any additional security concerns at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I further asked whether since your testimony in the second case you ever, either you yourself or your lawyer, contacted VWS in relation to any security concerns. The answer was that you had not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know who the individual was from their section whom I talked to, but I think that during my discussions before the special court in Belgrade with Judge Dilparic that I referred to earlier on, there was somebody who appeared to be taking notes as well. But I don't know what his actual position was, what his function was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will verify whether anyone of the Tribunal was present during those conversations. But at least after that you did not contact, although there have been frequent contact about all kind of travel arrangements. The answer by VWS to your letter starts: "Firstly, we wish to apologise for the frequent phone calls you have received over the last few weeks." So there has been frequent contact. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There have been frequent contact but they had to do with the date on which I was supposed to appear. Initially, it was the 22nd then the 27th then the 29th so it only had to do with the date of my appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did not raise any security concerns or you didn't ask for any further contacts in relation to security concerns at that moment, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't because I realized it was futile and I would not be getting in touch with them for any reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has gained an impression of the communications between the witness and the Tribunal and does not consider the cause of these events such that we should not at this moment hear the testimony of the witness. Mr. Groome, there have been a few matters, we'll first ask the witness whether he can point at any portions of his statement which he considers to be not in accordance with the truth. That's another matter of whether they are complete or not. The Chamber will defer its decision on admission of any 92 ter statements at this moment, we'll first -- we'll first hear the answer of the witness. Witness JF-026, could you tell us when reading the 114 paragraphs or the portion that you were able to read, are there any portions which you could point at as saying that they are not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are some points which do not reflect my evidence since an audio recording was made at the time and a written summarised version of it, I signed it as it was at the time. My lawyer Tomic was present, and well, I signed it simply because we had very little time before my flight. And if I look at point 90 here, the Orthodox bishop is referred to here as an archbishop, so that's just one point. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us one by one. We have pointed that you say 90, the bishop is an archbishop. That is, let me see, I have some difficulties in finding any -- even a bishop in number 90. Do you have it in front of you? Could you tell us what line? I can't find the bishop in paragraph 90, could you assist us, Witness JF-026?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My mistake, 102. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would say the Zvornik-Tuzla bishop, Kacavenda, is an archbishop. That is -- could we take it any further comments on matters which are not true. By the way an archbishop is still a bishop, so to that extent it's not untrue but that's a clarification. I'm not seeking at this moment, this kind of clarification, but I'm primarily looking at portions of your statement where you say this is wrong. Any other portions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Point 32, paragraph 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are with you, 32. What is wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that where security services mentioned it should state either civilian or military. Evidently at the time the Prosecutor knew the point he was driving and I didn't know what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Security service. Let me see, I find a reference to state security in the third line, then I see another reference to the Serbian state security in the sixth line, but let me see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I'm sorry, there is no mention of the Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if there's a translation issue, then I need to have a look at the original as well. Is there any translation issue there, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is, Your Honour. In the signed version which is a Serbian version it reads "security service" which is a general term, quite indefinite. Whereas in paragraph 32 in translation it is written "Serbian state security."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, that word appears twice, is in both cases is it your position that a reference is made to security services, that it means both on the second to third line and also in the sixth line? Is both instances a general reference to security services as far as you are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's what it reads, from the Serbian state security.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or rather, interpreter's correction: It says Serbian security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is different from the Serbian state security as it reads in your translation. And in my understanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That apparently is a matter which needs further attention as far as translation is concerned. Witness JF-026, any other instance where --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 37, yes. Tell us what is not right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here I'm explaining my acquaintance with Rade Kostic. This is something that I explained and you can hear it in the audiotape, that Rade Kostic was from Zvornik and I knew him at the time when he was -- I knew him from the time when he lived in Darda in Croatia, but that I knew that later on he became an employee of the state security service, that's not true because I never was in touch with him while he was in that capacity. I was never in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a part of what the witness just said that has not been interpreted. Can he please answer the question again so that I do not suggest what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you guide us in relation to what Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, line 24, after he said that he lived in Darda, he also said who he was a member of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Kostic told me that he was a high functionary of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is on the record as well. It might be that this is a matter which could be verified also on the basis of documentary evidence, but we may have two issues, first translation, second content. You said you listened to the audio, and have you explained it properly in the audio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That wasn't important in those proceedings. Nobody ever asked me anything about that. I'm talking about the audiotape that was made when the summary of this text was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear to me. We have had no access to that audio, but I take it that Mr. Groome, you could help us if there's any need to further listen to that audio. Could you tell us what else you noted as being incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bullet point 44, paragraph 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is where I speak why Marko Pavlovic came to Zvornik, what I wanted to say here is that I had met Pavlovic in Darda in the Republic of Serbian Krajina, where he was the TO commander for the town of Darda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you knew Mr. Pavlovic because you had met --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That you had met him in Darda where he was the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Baranja, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing here says you met him in any other way, but this apparently then adds to how you got acquainted with Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also bullet point 90. Nine zero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that I took cigarettes to the MUP members -- members ever the MUP of Republika Srpska in Bratunac. No, I apologise, everything is fine here. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next item where you say things are not in accordance with the truth or reality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this basically is all that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So apart from the fact that you think that some of the -- that part of the statement you made needs perhaps further clarification, these are the clear inaccuracies which you identified. Now, did I understand you well that you had an opportunity to read this before you came to court and that you had an opportunity to, although briefly, read it over the half-hour break as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, as far as the audios are concerned, I do understand that you received yesterday an audio of the -- of your testimony in the second case. Were you able to listen to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll not further deal with it in much detail, but did you find clear inaccuracies in that audio of your second -- of your testimony in the second case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I was informed, but please correct me when it's not true, that you were offered at an earlier stage to listen to the audio of the testimony in the first case, but when this was offered to you that you had told the person offering it to you, which was someone of VWS, that you were already in the possession of that first audio and that you had listened to it already. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. But I thought that that concerned the audio recording of this summary. I didn't realise that we are talking about the audiotape from the first trial. It is, however, correct that I was offered to listen to some other audiotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you are talking about the audio of the -- of this summary, are you talking about the audio of an interview, the interview which resulted in your 2008 statement, is that what you are referring to, or is there any other audio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me tell you, there are a few, but I meant the year 2008 when a summary was finally made of all of my statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you gave that, in 2008, statement, was that audio recorded, that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, if there would be any challenge to whether the witness would have said as is found in his written statement, would that audio recording, is that available?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Just so the record is correct, it's a video, so it has video plus audio recording. Your Honour, I think it's also important to note throughout that interview the witness's lawyer sat at his side and advised him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that the litigated video, was that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, that's then clear which gives the opportunity to verify whether this statement as we find it on paper is accurately reflects what was said during that interview. Under the present circumstances also in view of the answers given by the witness, the Chamber allows Mr. Groome to proceed. The Chamber does not yet decide on admission of the statement or any of the transcripts. The Chamber reserves its position as far as whether at any moment the Chamber would prefer to hear the evidence more in a viva voce way rather than by referring to a statement or transcript, but at the same time allows you, Mr. Groome, to proceed on the basis of an assumption that 92 ter might appropriately be applied here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: JF-026, you have just in an answering Judge Orie's questions described a number of corrections that you wish to make to your statement from 2008 and to your testimony in the second case. Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of your prior evidence if it's taken in conjunction with your corrections which you've just stated on the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any objection to this question, you would have to limit yourself ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask you to allow me to say two sentences. This all sounds very artificial -- please allow me to say two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I'm here in charge, would you please keep that in mind. Do you speak any English, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your earphones off until I -- yes. Mr. Petrovic, I wanted to instruct the witness to take his earphones off. Under those circumstances, you should patiently wait until I have finished what I wanted to say, and then I would have decided on your application to give two sentences. You may address the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I just wanted to say, to ask the Trial Chamber to look at the portion of his testimony today, pages 30. Over there he expressed his view that his previous statements were given under specific circumstances which influenced truthfulness of those statements. So I'm not sure we can proceed having that in mind on this basis. And I'm sorry, Your Honour, for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, that is exactly what we considered when we said that the Chamber will not yet decide on admission of the 92 ter statement and something you have not heard often from my mouth is that the Chamber would consider it's possible that at any stage we would rather have the evidence be elicited as viva voce. So that's exactly -- these are the kind of reasons which we had on our mind when we decided to take this course. This having been considered by the Chamber, we will invite the witness to put his earphones on again, and Mr. Groome may proceed. Witness. Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: JF-026, you did not have a chance to answer the question. So that there's no confusion, now that you've taken the solemn declaration do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of the statement you gave in 2008 and your testimony in the second case if it's taken in conjunction with the corrections you've just identified for Judge Orie?

utterances.speaker: JF-026
utterances.text: I believe that those circumstances were different then and I must admit that we played tactical games at the time. All of us did, and you can understand this any way you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm asking you to confine yourself to the very specific questions that Judge Orie asked you with respect to your 2008 statement. Is there anything in that statement, apart from what you've already told us, which is not the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to leap to my feet, but I feel compelled to object to the continued questions. I think in our submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to -- let's try to cut those matters short. Witness JF-026, I asked you whether you had reviewed your 2008 statement, whether you went through it again and what was not in accordance with the truth. You gave us a few -- you gave us a few comments on the content. You took us through the various paragraphs. Now, apart from whether your answers were always complete, are there any other matters in that statement where, reading it again, you say it's not true what is stated there, either because you didn't say it or because what you said is not in accordance with the truth. Are there any other such matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, most of the things contained in here are the things that I did say. However, I still believe that this summary can provide a completely different picture to what I actually said. Having said that, I did say what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you lie or did you speak the truth when you -- I'm not asking you whether you said everything, but whether you specifically did not tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can call it the truth or not. I told you that all of us who were close to the events played tactical games in order to put ourselves in the OTP's good books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then tell us where you played a tactical game which makes your statement untruthful apart from the portions you addressed already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the -- that would apply to the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say it's all untruthful, the whole statement is untruthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. 90 per cent of it is truthful and adjusted to what the OTP wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us one example where you told us you told anything where you thought that the OTP wanted to hear something which differs from what is the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The example was the second statement where I mention Mr. Zoran Subotic. He was the deputy minister in Milosevic's government and he was also a very close collaborator of Seselj and when I said that Zoran Subotic had been mobilised by the JNA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second statement, are you talking about the one that had the 114 paragraphs, the bullet points, this one, which you reviewed during the break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where that is mentioned. I don't know the number, and that gentleman is mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's actually bullet point 65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
